fda.license_documents: 510(k) summaries are written by device sponsors and posted by the US FDA. FDA's website policy treats FDA-created content as public domain unless marked (https://www.fda.gov/about-fda/about-website/website-policies). Whether each sponsor-written passage is itself free of restriction was not checked. This repository stores only facts from them (counts and printed percentages) with the document URL, and no text.

holdout.how_found: Europe PMC REST search (https://www.ebi.ac.uk/europepmc/webservices/rest/search) for open-access articles from 2024 and 2025 whose reported license is CC BY, with queries on confusion matrices, large language model exam accuracy, diagnostic sensitivity and specificity, and random-sample audits. 1,964 articles listed, 937 full texts read as text (fullTextXML), 93 contained a sentence pairing a count out of a total with a percentage near the words accuracy, sensitivity, specificity, precision, recall or correct. Claims were taken from 30 of them, at most five per paper. The vendor page was found by web search for AI-text-detector benchmarks; of the six vendor, blog and model-card pages opened for counts, only this one printed counts.
holdout.stored: counts, the printed percentage, and a short description in the repository's own words; no article text. Each claim carries its source URL.
holdout.license_note: Facts (counts and rates) are stored with attribution to the article. The articles are CC BY per Europe PMC; the vendor page is not licensed for reuse, so only its printed numbers are stored.
